# THE SECOND BELL — editorial facts and complete manuscript

## Publication identity

- Title: THE SECOND BELL
- Optional subtitle: A story in two voices
- Publication language: English
- Credit fields: title and optional subtitle
- Cover expression: typography, abstract graphics and ambiguous original illustration
- Recurring object identity: cracked brass bell, as depicted in bell-identity.png
- Front wording: THE SECOND BELL; optional A story in two voices
- Spine wording: THE SECOND BELL
- Spine reading direction: top to bottom
- Back-cover blurb: One cinema. Two voices. One last night. A locked door, an empty case and a familiar sound leave Mara and Ivo listening for different answers.

# THE SECOND BELL — original manuscript

## M1 | Mara | 22:10 | Light under the door

At ten past ten, light still lay beneath the projection-room door. The audience had gone. I had counted their programmes into the recycling box, each one folded to the same unhappy face on the poster. Upstairs, something knocked twice against the wall.

I tried the handle. Locked. Ivo's coat hung beside the stairs, rain dropping steadily from its sleeve into a paper cup. He had told me he would be home before the last credits.

The brass bell belonged on the counter. It had been cracked since before I worked here, and nobody rang it. Yet from somewhere above me came its small, uneven note. I put down my keys so they would not announce that I was listening.

## I1 | Ivo | 22:10 | A place to put the rain

The cup was too small for the water in my coat. I left it anyway. Upstairs the projector fan made its patient sound, although the screen in the auditorium was already blank. I did not want Mara to find me standing beside an empty case.

On the table were two strips of masking tape. One said KEEP. The other had lost every letter except an M. I turned that strip face down. The little brass bell was in my pocket, wrapped in a square of curtain cloth. I had taken it from the counter at nine.

When its rim touched the handrail, the cloth failed to soften the sound. I stood still. Below, a ring of keys stopped moving. Neither of us called the other's name.

## M2 | Mara | 22:26 | The empty circle

At twenty-six past ten I found the film case open on the landing. Its circular hollow held one pale thread and no reel. The label on the lid was my mother's handwriting. Not her name: the private way she crossed a seven, twice, as if once could not be trusted.

Ivo had asked to borrow the case that morning. He had said there was a label to repair. Now the lid lay in a wedge of light and the narrow corridor smelled of warm dust.

I reached for the thread but did not lift it. If I carried it downstairs, it would become something I had found. Left where it was, it could still be something I had misunderstood. Beyond the locked door, a chair scraped once across the floor.

## I2 | Ivo | 22:26 | The missing word

I had practised an explanation on the bus and forgotten it on the stairs. By twenty-six past ten, every useful sentence sounded like an excuse. The empty case could go back to Mara. What had been inside it could not go back to the place I had found it.

I pushed the chair away from the door. The key was still in the lock on my side. A thread from the curtain cloth caught on my cuff, and I pulled until it broke. I wondered whether she had noticed the missing bell.

There was room on the blank tape for a new label. I wrote the date and stopped before the name. From the corridor came the careful silence of somebody choosing not to knock. I was grateful for it, which made it worse.

## M3 | Mara | 22:40 | After the second bell

At twenty to eleven the door opened. Ivo held the reel in both hands. A paper note lay across it, written in the same double-crossed sevens. My mother had asked him to mend the torn leader and show the film to me after the cinema's final night. She had not asked him to keep it secret for ever.

He set the cracked bell beside the projector. On the little screen, my mother entered the old foyer carrying that same bell. She rang it twice, laughed at the wrong note and waved somebody out of the frame. A child took one step towards her. The child was me.

The pale thread had come from the cloth around the bell. Nothing had been stolen. I sat in the chair I had heard moving, and let the film begin again.

## I3 | Ivo | 22:40 | The label I could finish

By twenty to eleven I had run out of things to postpone. I opened the door and gave Mara the reel before I tried to explain. Her mother's note was easier to believe than anything I could have said. I had repaired a torn leader, not altered the pictures. The promise had been to wait until closing night, not to make Mara afraid.

The bell returned to the light. On the film it rang twice; beside the projector it kept its silence. Mara sat down without asking me to leave. When the child stepped into the picture, she leaned forward.

I finished the label with her mother's name, then put it on the empty case. We would need somewhere safe for the reel when the room went dark. This time I left the key outside the door.

steps.userMessage:
THE SECOND BELL | Reading structure and typography for a suspense novel in two voices

Design the cover and reading structure for THE SECOND BELL, a literary suspense novel following Mara and Ivo during one cinema's closing night. The first reading follows M1 → I1 → M2 → I2 → M3 → I3, pairing their accounts at 22:10, 22:26 and 22:40. After I3, readers can follow Mara through M1 → M2 → M3 or Ivo through I1 → I2 → I3. The supplied manuscript fixes the events and headings; chapter presentation, typography and abstract cover imagery are open. Introduce the resolution at M3, then develop it through I3 and the reread map.

The edition is a 120 × 160 mm perfect-bound paperback with 176 interior pages on 80 gsm Munken Print Cream 15, an uncoated cream paper with a sheet thickness of 0.12 mm. Its 88 leaves give a spine width of 88 × 0.12 = 10.56 mm. The cover wrap measures 250.56 × 160 mm before the 3 mm outer bleed. The 22 supplied positions are the designed sample positions within this edition: front cover 1; entry 2–3; Mara opener 4–5; Ivo opener 6–7; six story spreads 8–19; reread map 20–21; back cover 22. Interior sample folios retain these numbers. Print "THE SECOND BELL" on the front and spine, with spine lettering running from top to bottom; the optional front subtitle is "A story in two voices". The complete back-cover copy is "One cinema. Two voices. One last night. A locked door, an empty case and a familiar sound leave Mara and Ivo listening for different answers."

Audience: adult literary readers who reconstruct events from different characters' clues, with the editorial and design teams using the work to approve the reading experience and book design.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the complete manuscript, exact headings, sample allocations, reading paths and reveal stages. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable's proportion, format and stage. cover-envelope.png supplies the measured cover geometry and binding calculation. bell-identity.png establishes the cracked brass bell's appearance wherever that object is depicted. bookstore-reference.png supplies the atmosphere of a physical bookshop's new-release table.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page layout specification and reading-rules sheet stating trim, extent, paper, spine calculation, column count, margins, type sizes, actual font names, viewpoint labels, reading paths and the M3 reveal gate
2. Two cover views: one flat back–spine–front wrap with bleed and dimension annotations, and one front-cover thumbnail
3. One six-page opening-sequence document containing entry/contents 2–3, Mara opener 4–5 and Ivo opener 6–7
4. Six complete story spreads, one each for M1, I1, M2, I2, M3 and I3, with all assigned manuscript paragraphs and navigation
5. One reread-map spread for positions 20–21, connecting both character paths and the three paired times
6. One book mockup image showing the closed book and an open M1 spread
7. One 10-second book preview video using the delivered cover and M1 spread
8. One design presentation of at least 8 pages, reusing the specification, cover views, opening sequence, six story spreads, reread map and mockup

Acceptance:
- The specification establishes 120 × 160 mm trim, 176 interior pages, 80 gsm Munken Print Cream 15 at 0.12 mm per sheet, and the 88 × 0.12 = 10.56 mm spine calculation. Repeat the trim, extent and spine width in the wrap's annotation area and presentation; repeat the specification's column count, margins, type sizes and font names in the presentation.
- The wrap, thumbnail, mockup and video carry THE SECOND BELL on their visible front covers. The wrap has a 120 mm back, 10.56 mm spine and 120 mm front in that order, plus 3 mm outer bleed; its spine title reads top to bottom and its back carries the complete fixed blurb. The thumbnail preserves a readable complete title at the catalogued display size.
- The opening sequence presents M1 → I1 → M2 → I2 → M3 → I3 as the first-reading path and introduces Mara and Ivo through their names and readable viewpoint labels. Its contents give each story ID and starting sample folio: M1 8, I1 10, M2 12, I2 14, M3 16 and I3 18.
- Each of the six story spreads contains its complete assigned text, exact heading, ID, viewpoint, time and allocated folios. The specification's viewpoint labels and layout rules recur across all six. Print "Next" with the next ID and starting folio on M1 through M3; I3 points to "Reread", pages 20–21.
- The wrap, thumbnail, opening sequence, M1, I1, M2, I2, mockup and video use information available before M3. The mother's instruction, repaired film leader, childhood film and conclusion that nothing was stolen first become available in M3; I3 and the reread map develop that resolution. The reread map labels both character paths as reading after I3 and pairs M1/I1 at 22:10, M2/I2 at 22:26 and M3/I3 at 22:40.
- The mockup reproduces the delivered cover and M1, and the 10-second video uses those same designs. The presentation contains at least 8 pages, identifies the 22 positions as the design sample within the 176-page edition, and demonstrates the first-reading route, both rereading routes and the transition into M3 using the delivered pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
